stem: Siddharth learns that in sexual reproduction each gamete carries half of a parent's genetic material. A male gamete and a female gamete then join at fertilisation.

parts.text: Which claim correctly describes what this arrangement does?

options.text: Half-material gametes prevent genetic instructions from doubling each generation, while fertilisation still mixes information from two parents.
Sexual reproduction is the same as asexual copying, so gametes never carry half the material.
Fertilisation still mixes two parents even if each gamete carried a full set, and doubling never matters.
Fertilisation comes first, and only afterward do parents form half-material gametes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Each gamete carries half so joining restores a full set without doubling every generation, while still mixing two parents.

teacher.key_rationale: Half-material gametes avoid doubling; fertilisation mixes two parents. Treating sexual as asexual, dropping the half-step, or reversing the order of gamete formation and fertilisation all miss the hinge.
